Approver provenance — where the human’s identity survives

Every cell is derived at render time by scanning each real artifact for a key that DENOTES an approver, so this table self-corrects: fix the actor and the next regeneration flips these to kept. Key-based, not value-based, on purpose — in this scenario the approving principal and the requesting actor-id are the same string, so scanning values would mistake the commit fact’s :actor field for approval provenance.

OpRecordApproved byHanded to store (:payload)Registry recordLedger commit fact
:fee/drawdownDRAWDOWN-000000op-1kept · :approved-bydroppeddropped
:carry/distributeCARRY-000000op-1kept · :approved-bydroppeddropped
:guideline/discloseGUIDELINE-000000op-1kept · :approved-bydroppeddropped

Measured defect. fundmgmt.operation DOES hand the approver to the store — :request-approval puts :approved-by into the :payload, and fundmgmt.store/commit-record! DOES read :payload (not :value). The identity is lost one layer further down: fundmgmt.registry/register-fee-drawdown, register-carry-distribution and register-guideline-disclosure take positional arguments and are never passed :approved-by, so it is dropped before the immutable record is built.

The append-only ledger is blind to it too: an approved :committed fact has exactly the same key set as the AUTO-committed mandate fact, so the ledger cannot distinguish a human approved this from this auto-committed.

The :approval-granted fact exists only in the graph’s in-memory :audit channel for the duration of the run — fundmgmt.operation’s :commit node appends only the commit fact, so no record of WHO approved a real cash movement reaches the SSoT at all.
